label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame
starts too bright: an attack in its envelope

R1.reason: Frames 0 to 11 read as a radial burst: a bright cluster of blobs that spreads, with spiky rays in frames 4 to 7 (the rays are clearest in 4 to 7). That is closer to an explosion or puff than to a sludge spit splashing. There are no droplets leaving the centre or falling back, and the streaks and cluster give the shape of a fireball, not a splash.

R2.reason: Each frame is 64 x 64, as the brief's sprite size needs. The effect fills the central 60 to 70% of each cell, and the border is clean (border max 0.035, mean 0), so nothing is cut off at the edges.

R3.reason: The colour is a saturated lime-yellow that goes near white-yellow at the centre of frames 1 to 4. The brief's sludge is grey-green and muted, so this reads brighter and more yellow than sludge would. The green-yellow hue is in the right family, which keeps it from a 0.

R4.reason: The frame count (12) and the end (last 0, dark at frame 11) match the class, and the peak at 0.36 is inside the class range of 0.22 to 0.71. But the first frame is 0.82 bright, outside the class's 0 to 0.22, so the sprite starts too bright and has an attack it should not have. Jitter is 1.68, above the class's 1.04 to 1.48: the blob layout changes from frame to frame (compare 0 to 1 and 6 to 7), so it flickers instead of moving coherently.

R5.reason: The file is fw_spit.spr, as the sprite is named. It is additive and parallel, with 12 frames at 64 x 64, and no measure shows a fault in its type or format. I could not check the type and format of the file it replaces, so that comparison is not in this judgement.
